correctness.rationale: The pure-death transition chain has independent Geom(p_k) holding times and mean Σ1/p_k, variance Σ(1-p_k)/p_k². Under Σ(p_k-k/M)<=B, strict convexity of Σ1/p_k and KKT derivative -1/p_k² yield unique clipped water-filling p_k=max(k/M,c); budget function is continuous and increasing, with upper cap c<1. Writing K≈Mc yields K~sqrt(2BM), c~sqrt(2B/M), leading mean M[1/2 log M +1 -1/2 log(2B)+o(1)], and variance two equal leading tail contributions totaling sqrt(2/B) M^(3/2). Geometric third absolute moments sum O_B(M²), yielding Lyapunov CLT on scale M^(3/4). Independently checked exact rational M=100,B=1/2 threshold c=21/200 and budget, and strict local convex comparison; source verifier was inspected but was not taken as an all-M proof.
residual_risks: Aggregate statewise TV budget is not a per-step numerical error guarantee; p_M=1 fixed.

value.rationale: Optimizing a finite aggregate budget of signed rounding bias is a natural exact resource-allocation question. Its unique policy produces a nontrivial change both to the leading absorption-time scale and the limit distribution, offering a precise benchmark for quantized-descent models beyond a routine KKT calculation.
residual_risks: Practical low-precision hardware bias is not equivalent to the modelled transition probabilities.

limitations: Fixed positive B, statewise total-variation budget, scalar integer quadratic only.
The Gaussian limit does not extend automatically to B approaching 0 with M.
